name: mixed-self-distillation-pilot-v1
status: proposal, before any data; code and plan go to the orchestrator before any fit
label: descriptive pilot, training side for Room 2; no confirmatory claim; the Room 2 v2 held-out set is never read
question: Does cloning a Room 1 policy on Room 2 demonstrations together with its own recorded Room 1 play, fitted to its own action probabilities (mixed self-distillation), keep its Room 1 held-out skill, where mixing in the Room 1 demonstrations did not (mixed-imitation pilot, branch B)? And does PPO on Room 2 afterwards wear that skill down?
why: The coverage-ceiling pilot (branch P, docs/results/coverage-ceiling-pilot.json) showed that a fresh network fitted to a donor's own probabilities on its recorded play plays Room 1 at a median 0.92 of the donor's margin over the floor, against 0.12 for copying the demonstrations on the same kind of states. The orchestrator's result review (2026-09-27) approved this as the next step: the same targets, now mixed with Room 2 learning from the donor's own weights.
decisions_it_may_inform: whether mixed self-distillation at the cloning step keeps the Room 1 skill, and whether the PPO stage then needs its own Room 1 anchor
whether later rooms need a live recording per donor or whether the existing demonstration datasets suffice (the D-k rung, descriptive)
the rough size of the Room 1 effect, for a later power estimate
decisions_it_may_not_inform: anything else, including which seeds, clone seeds, checkpoints, mixing ratio or Room 2 settings a later experiment uses; one striking run does not set the next design
changed_from_mixed_imitation_pilot: only the Room 1 part of the imitation data: the donor's own recorded play replaces the Room 1 demonstrations, and its targets are the donor's own action probabilities (computed from the --init-from weights before any fitting) instead of the demonstrated actions. Everything else is held fixed.

held_fixed.donors: config/retention-pilot.json donors: Room 1 varied-start seeds 3 to 6, same checkpoints and sha256, same before values
held_fixed.room2_data: runs/clone/chapter-1-room-2/20260924-014351/dataset.npz with config/demonstrations-room2-v2.json and config/heldout_starts-room2-v2.json (overlap check only); split alone with seed k, so the same 5 held-back Room 2 routes as M-k, R-k and H2 B-k
held_fixed.fine_tuning: the mixed-imitation pilot's M-k command with --init-from <SD-k clone> and --run-dir runs/train/mixed-self-distillation-pilot-SD-k<k>: rew-v2, shaping 2.0, 500,000 steps, checkpoints every 100,000, --stall-frames 296, --seed 40 + k, Room 2 canonical starts only
held_fixed.measurement_commands: Room 1 held-out: scripts/evaluate_heldout.py --checkpoint <zip> --starts config/heldout_starts.json --repeats 1 --seed 20260920 (aggregates only); Room 2 canonical: scripts/evaluate_checkpoint.py --task-definition config/room2.json --episodes 50 --seed 20260924 --reward-version rew-v2 --shaping-scale 2.0
held_fixed.floors: the retention pilot's floors, reused (docs/results/retention-pilot.json): clone floor 0.142 for the post-clone point, final floor 0.205 for the fine-tuned points
held_fixed.reference: the imitation-only reference (Room 1-only clones on the demonstrated actions, mean 0.122), reported beside every clone

room1_data.source: the coverage-ceiling pilot's four recordings, reused as they are (no new live recording): 25 stochastic canonical episodes per donor, seed 20260926, recorded at d1e5794, each verified by --mix-play against the --init-from sha256 (celeste_rl/policy_play.py: same donor, unchanged dataset, same task, clean tree, attributable, canonical starts only)
room1_data.split: each recording is split alone with seed k: 6 of 25 episodes held back, the same 6 as S-play-k (checked offline 2026-09-27: k0 [2, 4, 10, 11, 19, 24], k1 [1, 7, 15, 17, 20, 21], k2 [7, 14, 16, 18, 20, 21], k3 [0, 12, 13, 15, 17, 23]; fitted frames 4,472 / 8,619 / 4,307 / 5,863, equal to S-play-k)
room1_data.targets_check: checked offline 2026-09-27: the targets --mix-play computes from the --init-from weights are bit-identical to those distill_policy.py computed from the loaded donor for S-play-k

runs.design: SD-k for k = 0 to 3: donor seed 3 + k; mixed clone seed k; fine-tuning seed 40 + k. Nominally paired with M-k, R-k and S-play-k.
runs.sd_clone_command: scripts/clone_room1.py --task-definition config/room2.json --dataset runs/clone/chapter-1-room-2/20260924-014351/dataset.npz --demonstrations config/demonstrations-room2-v2.json --heldout config/heldout_starts-room2-v2.json --mix-play default <recording of donor 3 + k> --mix-targets donor --room-weighting equal --routes-only --holdout 0.25 --epochs 300 --batch-size 64 --learning-rate 0.001 --no-play --seed <k> --init-from <donor> --init-from-sha256 <donor sha256>
runs.plans: clones fitted by hand with a durable log; then a mechanically generated, committed training plan pinning the four SD-k clone hashes (dry run first); then a committed evaluation plan pinning every checkpoint, with the analyzer committed before any evaluation

d_k_rung.role: descriptive only, never a branch; reported beside SD-k
d_k_rung.what: D-k: the Room 1 demonstration states with the donor's own probabilities as targets, mixed with the same Room 2 data (no new code: --mix-room with --mix-targets donor, reviewed in 58590f2). With M-k (demonstration states, demonstrated actions) and SD-k (donor play, donor targets) it forms a ladder.
d_k_rung.clone_command: scripts/clone_room1.py --task-definition config/room2.json --dataset runs/clone/chapter-1-room-2/20260924-014351/dataset.npz --demonstrations config/demonstrations-room2-v2.json --heldout config/heldout_starts-room2-v2.json --mix-room default config/demonstrations.json config/heldout_starts.json runs/clone/20260925-221134/dataset.npz --mix-targets donor --room-weighting equal --routes-only --holdout 0.25 --epochs 300 --batch-size 64 --learning-rate 0.001 --no-play --seed <k> --init-from <donor> --init-from-sha256 <donor sha256>
d_k_rung.measured: the post-clone point only (Room 1 held-out and Room 2 canonical); no PPO stage
d_k_rung.reading: if D-k keeps about as much as SD-k, later rooms may not need a live recording per donor; if it keeps much less, they do. Descriptive; any such choice goes to the orchestrator and the owner.

measurements.primary_room1: Room 1 held-out route-macro and state-weighted success for every SD-k clone and every step checkpoint (100k to 500k), all evaluated, no best checkpoint; retained share (after - floor) / (before - floor), clone floor for the clone, final floor for the steps
measurements.comparison: M-k and R-k at every point, S-play-k and S-demo-k for the clone point, the imitation-only reference; described across the four runs
measurements.per_room_imitation: held-back input and frame accuracy per room for each SD-k and D-k clone (recorded by clone_room1.py); Room 2 against M-k and R-k; Room 1 as agreement with the donor on its own held-back episodes
measurements.weights: the per-frame weight of each room under equal weighting, recorded per clone (results.json mix.per_frame_weight)
measurements.secondary_room2: Room 2 canonical clears of 50 for each SD-k and D-k clone and each SD-k final; training clear rate per 100k window and first 50k window at 50%, beside M-k and R-k
measurements.critic_record: explained variance over the first 10 PPO updates for SD-k beside M-k

aggregates_only: The Room 1 held-out set already carries Phase 3B and the retention, mixed-imitation and coverage-ceiling pilots; it is treated as a development set and only aggregate success per checkpoint is reported, never per-route or per-state results. The fresh Room 1 v2 set comes before any claim beyond descriptive.

decision_branches.measure: median Room 1 route-macro retained share of the four SD-k clones against the clone floor 0.142; later points against the final floor 0.205
rules_in_order: K (keeps): the median SD-k clone share is at least 0.5. Run the PPO stage. Then K-hold: the median share at 500k is within 0.25 of its after-cloning value, and the Room 2 finals clear at least 45 of 50 in at least 3 of 4 runs (M-k finals: 48 to 50); read as 'mixed self-distillation keeps the skill through Room 2 learning, for now', and the next step is the fresh Room 1 v2 set before any claim. K-decay: the median share at 500k is more than 0.25 below its after-cloning value; cloning-time anchoring is not enough, and the next step is an anchor inside PPO. K-cost: neither (Room 1 holds but fewer than 3 of 4 Room 2 finals clear 45 of 50); reported as a Room 2 cost, and the owner and the orchestrator choose.

Partial: the median SD-k clone share is from 0.2 to below 0.5. Room 2 imitation pulls the shared network away even with donor targets. Next: more Room 1 weight or fewer epochs; the owner and the orchestrator choose. No PPO stage.
Lost: the median SD-k clone share is below 0.2. Next: a weight anchor or frozen layers; the owner and the orchestrator choose. No PPO stage.
decision_branches.reported_beside_every_branch: Room 2 held-back imitation accuracy against M-k and R-k: a Room 1 gain that costs Room 2 learning is not a win

declared_confounds: Critic: the Room 1 value head is copied with the weights, as in M-k and R-k.

More Room 1 frames than M-k: 4,307 to 8,619 fitted play frames against 1,948 to 2,056 demonstration frames. Equal weighting keeps each room's total weight at half, so the per-frame Room 1 weight is lower than in M-k and each epoch has more frames (more gradient steps); both are recorded per clone.

The held-out starts lie within a few pixels of both the recorded play and the demonstration paths (orchestrator's coverage-ceiling review); a good result shows keeping the skill along known paths, not far generalisation.
Donor targets bundle 'the donor's choices' and 'soft probabilities' (coverage-ceiling review); this pilot does not separate them.
The recordings come from canonical starts only, and the 4 donors come from one recipe (Phase 3B arm B).
Single checkpoints swing by a few points (about 3 points of sampling noise); describe patterns across the four runs.
evaluation_code_check: before any evaluation, confirm that scripts/evaluate_heldout.py, scripts/evaluate_checkpoint.py and every celeste_rl module they import are unchanged since f26914d (the floor's evaluation commit); if anything changed, re-evaluate the floor in the same plan
generator_checks: the training-plan generator selects exactly one SD-k clone per k by: donor sha256; seed k; a clean commit; 300 epochs; mix.room_weighting equal; mix.targets donor; mix.states donor play; mix.play.dataset_sha256 equal to that donor's recording above. Any smoke-test clone (fewer epochs) can never match. D-k clones are selected the same way with mix.states demonstrations and mix.targets donor, for the evaluation plan only.
later: An anchor inside PPO (an extra loss keeping the policy's probabilities near the frozen donor's on recorded Room 1 frames) is designed in parallel, per the orchestrator's review, and reviewed on its own before any use.
cost: No live recording. 4 SD-k and 4 D-k clones on CPU, about 15 to 25 minutes each (about 2.5 hours). If branch K: 4 fine-tuning runs, about 35 minutes each. Evaluations: 8 clones on Room 1 and Room 2 (about 25 minutes), plus 20 Room 1 checkpoint and 4 Room 2 final evaluations if K (about 50 minutes). About 3 hours without PPO, about 6 hours with it.
